 Order
With the consent of the parties, the matter is heard finally.

2. The present appeal has been preferred by the appellant under Section 374(2) of the Cr.P.C. being aggrieved by the judgment of conviction and sentenced passed by the 1st Additional Sessions Judge,
Raisen District Raisen in S.T. No.154/2010 dated 29.07.2011, whereby the appellant was convicted under Section 354 and sentenced for one year R.I and fine of Rs. 500 in default to further undergo one month R.I.
3.

1st Additional Sessions Judge,
Raisen District Raisen
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As per the prosecution story, one Keshobai lodged the report against appellant at Police Station Sultanpur District Raisen registered as crime No.96/2010 under Section 342 and 376/511 of IPC on 23.04.2010 at 9 P.M.,
wherein he was alleged with the appellant tried to commit the rape upon the 8 years old daughter of the complainant at 8 p.m.

Upon the report and after investigation,
charge-sheet was filed and prosecution examined as many as 6 witnesses in the case.
4. Learned Sessions Court after considering the evidence of the witnesses, acquitted the accused from the charges punishable under Section 342 and 376 read with Section 511 of IPC.

However, he was convicted in offence under Section 354 of IPC and sentenced for one year R.I. and fine of Rs.
500/-.
The appellant remained in custody during trial for 120 days from 24.02.2010 to 26.08.2010.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant submits that appellant has falsely been implicated in the present case.
He has not committed any offence.
The evidence of the prosecution witnesses are not sufficient to convict the appellant.

The medical report is also not in support of prosecution and according to the medical examination, there is no external injury was found on the body of the victim, therefore, the appeal is allowed and judgment and sentence be set aside.

In alternate, the learned counsel for the appellant submits that looking to the facts that the incident was of year 2010 and the appellant was aged 22 years at the time of incident and he has already suffered 1/3 period of sentence, therefore, sentence be reduced.

6. Per contra, Panel Lawyer appearing on behalf of the respondent/State supported the judgment and argued that victim was specifically deposed against the appellant before the Court and her mother also supported the case of the prosecution who reached at the spot and is eye witness.
Even there are no allegation of commission of rape but the offence under Section 354 is duly proved.
He prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

7. After perusal of the record, it appears that the learned Sessions Court has not committed any error in convicting the appellant under Section 354 of the IPC as the statement of the victim and her mother are sufficient to prove the offence against the appellant and the judgment has been passed after the appreciation of evidence and the conviction is maintained.
8.
However, looking to the facts that at the time of incident, the appellant was of 22 years old young boy.

The incident took place in the year 2010 and the period 13 years have been passed, the appellant has already suffered custody of 124 days which is almost 1/3 of the sentence awarded by the Appellate Court.

9. Hence, I deem it proper to reduce the jail sentence to the appellant which has already been undergone by the appellant and accordingly jail sentences is reduced, however, the fine amount is enhanced to the extent of Rs.5000/-.
The appellant will deposit the same within a period of 1 month from today.
10. With the aforesaid, the appeal is partly allowed.

(VINAY SARAF) JUDGE R Sudesh vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152056172/
